ai.stableNodeKey: (outline) § subtitle#0

content.text: You keep two identical production environments, called blue and green. One of them serves all live traffic while the other sits idle¹; you deploy the new version to the idle one, test it there, and then move traffic over in one step². Because the old environment is still running, going back is the same one-step switch³. The cost is running twice the infrastructure during a release, which is why the idle environment is scaled down between releases⁴.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › How blue-green works § text#0

content.text:
¹ The idle environment is not serving live traffic.
 ² Traffic is switched in a single step after deployment and testing.
 ³ Reverting to the old version is a quick, single-step process.
 ⁴ To mitigate cost, the idle environment is scaled down when not in use.

content.text: You need the following in place before the first release:

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#0

content.text: Two identical environments,
orders-blue
and
orders-green
, with the same instance count, instance size and configuration.
A health endpoint,
GET /healthz
, that returns
only when the service can reach its database and its queue.

Database migrations that are backward compatible, so the old version keeps working against the new schema. This is a hard requirement: both versions share one database, and a rollback does not undo a migration.
Access to the load balancer's listener rules, because the switch is a change to which target group the listener forwards to.
A dashboard or query that shows the 5xx error rate per environment, so you can tell green's errors from blue's.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#1

content.text: If any migration is not backward compatible, do not use this procedure; split the migration into an additive release first and a cleanup release later.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#2

content.text: This section outlines the essential prerequisites for a successful release using the blue/green deployment strategy. Key requirements include identical environments, a robust health check, backward-compatible database migrations, load balancer access, and error rate monitoring.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Before you start § text#3

content.text: In this walkthrough blue is live and green is idle.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#0

content.text: Deploy version
to
orders-green
, using the same build artifact that passed staging rather than a fresh build. Expected result: all green instances report the new version, and blue still serves 100% of traffic.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#1

content.text: Apply the database migrations from the new release, once, from a single job rather than from every green instance at startup. Expected result: the migration job exits with code 0, and blue keeps serving requests without new errors, which confirms the change is backward compatible.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#2

content.text: Poll the health endpoint on every green instance until all of them return
. If any instance is still failing health checks after 10 minutes, stop here and roll back: tear down green and leave blue serving traffic. Nothing has been switched yet, so customers are unaffected.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#3

content.text: Send the smoke-test suite to green's internal address. Expected result: all smoke tests pass. If one fails, treat it like a failed health check and stop.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#4

content.text: Point the listener at the green target group. Expected result: within about 30 seconds, new requests are served by green, and blue receives no new connections.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#5
Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § code#0

content.text: Observe the 5xx error rate on green for 15 minutes after the switch. If the error rate rises above 2% at any point in that window, switch back: run the same command with
$BLUE_TG_ARN
, which returns all traffic to blue within about 30 seconds. If it stays at or below 2%, continue.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#6

content.text: Leave blue running, unchanged, for 24 hours. It is your rollback target until then.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#7

content.text: After 24 hours without a switch-back, scale blue down. Blue becomes the idle environment for the next release, with the roles reversed.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#8

content.text: If any green instance fails health checks after 10 minutes, roll back by tearing down green. Customers are unaffected.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#9

content.text: If any smoke test fails, roll back by tearing down green. Customers are unaffected.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#10

content.text: If the 5xx error rate on green rises above 2% within 15 minutes after the switch, switch traffic back to blue.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › Steps § text#11

content.text: This blue/green deployment strategy allows for zero-downtime deployments with immediate rollback capabilities.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service § text#1

content.text: A rollback before step 5 is cheap, because customers never saw green. A switch-back after step 5 is also fast, but requests that were in flight on green during the switch may fail and need a client retry. Neither kind of rollback reverts the database, which is why the backward-compatible migration requirement matters. Whichever way you roll back, record what failed before trying again, because a second attempt with the same build tends to fail the same way.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § rollback_considerations

content.text: Do not run the next release's migrations while blue is still on standby. If you do, the standby may no longer work against the schema, and the switch-back stops being a safe option.

ai.stableNodeKey: Blue-green deployment for the orders service › When things go wrong § migration_warning

content.text: This section highlights the implications of rollbacks at different stages of deployment and emphasizes the importance of backward-compatible database migrations. It also warns against running future migrations on a standby environment.
